incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, as amended, particularly Articles 128, 129 through 135, 148, 161-2, 172, 192, 208, 387, and 393, together with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 7 through 12, and the Regulations Governing Approval of Foreign Investment; the applicable statutory vehicle for the wholly foreign-owned enterprise is a company limited by shares wholly owned by a foreign corporate shareholder.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Services, Company Registration One-Stop Service; for foreign-investment approval, the Investment Commission, MOEA.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration of a Company Limited by Shares, accompanied by the approved and sealed Articles of Incorporation, the establishment meeting minutes, and the certified public accountant capital verification report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a company limited by shares under the Taiwan Company Act. For a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, however, the paid-up capital must equal the amount expressly approved by the Investment Commission, MOEA, and must be remitted from abroad into a temporary foreign-investment capital account maintained at a licensed bank in Taiwan. The funds must remain unencumbered and must be verified by an independent Taiwan CPA through a capital verification report before company registration is granted. Blocked escrow account rules: None. A share capital release is not conditioned on any escrow arrangement, but the remittance must be completed and verified prior to final registration approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN WFOE LTD A COMPANY LIMITED BY SHARES UNDER THE TAIWAN COMPANY ACT. RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors of CN WFOE Ltd, Taiwan (the "Company"), acting pursuant to the Taiwan Company Act and the Articles of Incorporation, hereby adopts the following resolutions as the First Board Resolution. 1. Share Capital Subscription and Issuance. The Board confirms that the authorized share capital of the Company is fixed in the amount approved by the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, and that all issued shares have been subscribed in full by the sole corporate shareholder at par value. The Board accepts such subscriptions and directs that the aggregate subscription consideration be remitted from abroad into the Company's foreign-investment capital account maintained at a licensed bank in Taiwan. The Chairperson and the Company's independent certified public accountant are authorized to obtain a capital verification report evidencing the receipt of paid-up capital and to file all required certificates with the competent registry. 2. Banking Authorization. The Board approves the opening of domestic New Taiwan Dollar and foreign currency bank accounts with a licensed financial institution in Taiwan. The Chairperson and the General Manager, acting jointly or severally, are authorized to open, operate, and manage bank accounts; to sign account opening forms; to execute credit and wire transfer instructions; to endorse checks; to initiate SWIFT wires; and to perform all treasury operations on behalf of the Company. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The Board adopts the place specified in the Articles of Incorporation, located at the address set forth in the Company's registration application, as the registered office of the Company in Taiwan. The Chairperson is authorized to execute any lease, consent, or authorization document delivered by the premises owner and to file any required notices with the MOEA Department of Commercial Services. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The Board appoints the individual listed as Director A as Chairperson and statutory representative; the individual listed as Director B as General Manager; and the individual listed as Director C as Company Secretary and Financial Officer. The Chairperson and General Manager shall exercise all powers delegated by the Taiwan Company Act and the Articles of Incorporation, including representing the

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (MOF), National Taxation Administration, Taiwan; the applicable local National Taxation Bureau for the WFOE's registered address; online portals: MOF eTax Portal and the E-Invoice Integration Service Platform
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Taiwan WFOE (wholly foreign-owned limited liability company): (1) Complete incorporation under the Taiwan Company Act through the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company and Commercial Registration Portal; if the ultimate investor is a mainland China entity, obtain prior approval from the Investment Commission, MOEA under the Foreign Investment Act. (2) Before commencing business, file the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Tax Registration Application with the local National Taxation Bureau (NTB); the NTB issues an 8-digit Tax Identification Number (TIN), which is also the Uniform Invoice Number. (3) If a foreign non-resident company has no fixed place of business in Taiwan but conducts Taiwan-source sales, it must appoint a local tax agent and register under the same tax registration procedure before collecting Business Tax. (4) Register as an exporter with the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance, if physical goods are to be exported; the same TIN is used for customs and VAT. (5) Register for electronic Uniform Invoice issuance through the E-Invoice Integration Service Platform and obtain Turnkey/API credentials. (6) Open a foreign exchange account with a domestic authorized bank for export proceeds repatriation and retain all corporate authorization documents, board resolutions, and apostilled/notarized certificates for the Taiwan tax file.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not apply a US-style check-the-box election. The WFOE is a resident profit-seeking enterprise taxed at entity level under the Income Tax Act; no pass-through or disregarded-entity election exists. Anti-hybrid and controlled-foreign-company rules apply to cross-border structures. For Business Tax, the value-added/non-value-added system is compulsory; no election to register as a different indirect tax payer type is available except the small-scale-business assessment at 1% for low-turnover operators.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (Business Tax) under the Business Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for tax registration; every profit-seeking enterprise must register with the National Taxation Bureau before commencing taxable activity. For the standard VAT/uniform-invoice regime, compulsory Uniform Invoice issuance applies once average monthly taxable sales exceed NT$200,000; below that threshold, an eligible small-scale business operator may be taxed at 1% and is not required to issue Uniform Invoices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan uses a post-sale e-invoice reporting model, not real-time fiscal clearance. Registered WFOE must issue Uniform Invoices for taxable B2B sales and transmit electronic Uniform Invoice data to the MOF E-Invoice Integration Service Platform through the Turnkey connection or approved API. The platform validates invoice numbering, business TIN matching, and time stamps; there is no government anti-fraud digital stamp. B2B e-invoices are reported within the legal filing period; B2C receipts are printed or transmitted with lottery random numbers. Non-compliance with e-invoice transmission triggers Business Tax Act penalties on the output tax and reduces input credit integrity.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, 0% VAT applies to (i) physical goods exported from Taiwan evidenced by a valid customs export declaration; (ii) B2B platform services supplied to a foreign enterprise if the service is not used or consumed within Taiwan; and (iii) cross-border B2B marketplace sales where the goods are shipped from Taiwan to a foreign buyer. The WFOE must retain evidence of the foreign counterparty, foreign place of use or benefit, physical export movement, and actual foreign exchange repatriation. Zero-rated sales retain refundable input VAT credits after offsetting output tax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic export entry/export report) issued by the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance
Bill of Lading for sea freight or Air Waybill for air freight, with port or airport of discharge outside Taiwan
Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and freight or insurance documents
B2B marketplace purchase order, sales contract, platform transaction log, and payment routing evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate or Export Proceeds Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate issued by an authorized foreign-exchange bank
Zero-rated Uniform Invoice / electronic Uniform Invoice record transmitted to the E-Invoice Integration Service Platform
Foreign enterprise status evidence (e.g., foreign company registration certificate or equivalent) for service/offshore platform supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau cross-matches customs export records, e-invoice zero-rating codes, foreign-exchange settlement records, ocean/air manifests, and platform transaction data. If the WFOE cannot prove physical exit, foreign counterparty identity, foreign usage, or timely repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days, the zero-rating claim is reversed and the 5% Business Tax is assessed with interest from the original due date. Under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, a false or unsupported zero-rating claim carries a penalty of up to five times the tax evaded; under the Tax Collection Act, the collection and assessment period may extend up to seven years for fraudulent concealment, and egregious cases are referred for criminal tax evasion prosecution. The tax authority may also suspend Uniform Invoice supply until the audit is resolved.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime with RMB current-account convertibility while maintaining robust capital-account controls. For a CN_WFOE_LTD, trade-related current account receipts and payments, including import/export settlement, freight, insurance, and platform transaction fees, are generally convertible through designated banks after documentary verification of genuine underlying trade. Capital account flows, however, are strictly regulated: foreign direct investment capital injection must be registered with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) and routed into a dedicated FDI capital account; voluntary conversion into RMB is permitted but must be supervised through a settlement-change account system to prevent idle fund speculation. Export proceeds are subject to the Exports Collection Verification System, requiring repatriation of all proceeds into China for verification against customs declarations; the WFOE may retain foreign exchange without forced surrender, but there is no automatic right to delay repatriation, and overdue collections trigger alarms. Dividend and profit remittances to the Taiwan shareholder require SAFE registration, an audited financial statement showing accumulated earnings, corporate income tax settlement certificate, and evidence that foreign exchange for remittance comes from legal operations. The practical effect is an asymmetric regime: current account flows are fast and liberalized, while capital account exits require pre-audit and are time-bound. The WFOE must keep perfect underlying transaction files, invoice log, customs records, and e-tax stamps or its designated bank will suspend FX settlement and clearing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds are required to be repatriated through designated foreign-exchange banks within 90 days after customs export declaration; trade-contract extended periods up to 180 days are allowed with application. All export receipts must enter a domestic Foreign Exchange Settlement Account and go through SAFE's electronic verification. The statutory surrender ratio is 0% as mandatory conversion to RMB has been abolished, allowing 100% retention in foreign currency or voluntary conversion to RMB at market rate. Failure to repatriate or late verification will trigger suspension of tax rebates and downgrade by the bank's foreign-exchange compliance rating.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Cross-border digital banking platforms and EMI challengers generally cannot act as primary deposit-taking institutions for a Chinese WFOE because China's commercial banking law requires bank licenses and SAFE only permits settlement through designated foreign-exchange banks. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, or Neat may be useful for outbound supplier payments but cannot replace the domestic RMB capital account or corporate bank account. Legal use requires partnership with a licensed Chinese bank and payment institution, for example Alipay cross-border, under PBOC and SAFE licenses; direct account opening with a foreign EMI is not legally viable as a primary settlement rail for this WFOE.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The WFOE's legal representative must appear physically at the bank's China branch for the initial KYC account-opening interview. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for RMB basic deposit accounts; notarized and legalized powers of attorney may be accepted for supplementary signatories, but the principal legal representative needs an in-person interview or, under certain bank policies, a secured video KYC with two-factor identity authentication. In all cases, PBOC anti-money-laundering directives require face-to-face identity confirmation for the legal representative and the primary financial controller, with passports, Taiwan Compatriot Permit (if applicable), business license, and company seal used for physical verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership chain extends through a Taiwan parent whose corporate registry may not fully disclose natural persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarized and apostilled certificate of incumbency, corporate registry extracts for every intermediate entity, signed UBO declaration identifying all natural persons holding more than 25% of shares, passport copies of UBOs, and, if listed, stock exchange ownership disclosure report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial registered capital injection from Taiwan routed through multiple intermediary banks creates source-of-funds ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide SAFE-approved FDI registration certificate, bank inward remittance notices, 12 months of source-of-wealth documentation including tax returns and audited financial statements of the Taiwan shareholder, bank reference letter from the remitting Taiwan bank, and a capital verification report issued by a licensed Chinese CPA firm within 30 days of injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: B2B cross-border marketplace payment flows with high volume and low ticket sizes may mask trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide master sales and purchase agreements, transaction-level e-invoices with tax invoice verification, customs declaration forms, logistics waybills including bill of lading or airway bill, and an independent due-diligence report confirming counterparties are not sanctioned, shell, or counterfeit entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax residence mismatch between the China WFOE and Taiwan shareholder triggers FATCA and CRS classification risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide Taiwan shareholder's tax resident certificate, CRS self-certification or W-8BEN-E, PRC tax residency certificate for the WFOE, board resolution approving tax filings, and transfer pricing documentation for all intercompany transactions with the Taiwan parent.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Before wiring, the WFOE must complete SAFE foreign direct investment registration at the local branch, open a dedicated FDI capital account at a designated bank, and mark the SWIFT remittance with purpose code for foreign direct investment capital injection together with the SAFE FDI registration reference number. After receipt, the designated bank converts the capital into RMB at spot rate if requested, transfers the funds to a RMB settlement account for operational use, and the CPA performs capital verification within 30 days. All withdrawals and usage must comply with SAFE Circular 19/2016, which restricts cash withdrawals and requires fund monitoring against the WFOE's approved business scope and registered purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for high-value supplier payments, subject to SAFE trade verification, tax withholding, and supporting documents including import contracts, customs declarations, tax invoices, and e-tax certificates. For larger or structured transactions, open an irrevocable commercial letter of credit at sight or use documentary collections such as documents against payment and documents against acceptance through the designated bank's trade finance desk. Cross-border RMB clearing can be used for eligible counterparties under SAFE's cross-border RMB rules, and all B2B marketplace balances collected through Alipay must be settled first into the WFOE's domestic settlement account before any outbound disbursement is executed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return (Income Tax Act Article 71)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance, Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: From May 1 to May 31 of the calendar year following the tax year (or within 5 months after close of a non-calendar fiscal year); E-filing arrears grace through June 1 in certain years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without tax liability: fixed penalty of NT$1,500 (approx. USD 47); with tax liability: late surcharge of 3% per month up to a maximum of 9%, plus one-month interbank interest; for willful failure after demand, additional fine up to NT$15,000; persistent non-filing triggers tax liens on bank deposits, asset attachment, and forced corporate dissolution via MOE/collection enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements, Business Report, and Profit Distribution Proposal; for companies with paid-in capital NT$30 million or above, CPA-Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' Meeting; Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOE) Company Registration Division for audited statement filing/inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be presented to shareholders within 6 months of fiscal-year end (by June 30 for a calendar-year company); audited statements of threshold companies must be filed with MOE within the same 6-month window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Company Act Articles 228 and 230, responsible persons failing to prepare or submit statements to shareholders are subject to MOE corrective orders, repeated fines of NT$10,000-50,000 (approx. USD 320-1,600) per violation, and in serious cases administrative dissolution under Company Act Article 10; certifying CPAs may be disciplined by the Financial Supervisory Commission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign-Investment Operation Report for WFOE (foreign investment registration maintenance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the close of each fiscal year (by June 30 for a calendar-year WFOE); also required within 15 days of any capital or shareholding change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file on time may trigger an administrative warning and a fine of up to NT$20,000 (approx. USD 635) per violation; recurring non-compliance may result in suspension or revocation of the foreign-investment approval, thereby jeopardizing tax preferences, foreign-exchange privileges, and legal operational standing, and ultimately leading to mandatory deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Major Shareholders/Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Registration and Annual Confirmation (Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOE) Company Electronic Registration System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after any share transfer or change in major shareholder/controller; annual confirmation is integrated with the foreign-investment annual report (due by June 30/within 6 months of FYE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false filing: MOE issues a rectification order and imposes a fine of NT$50,000 (approx. USD 1,587) per offense; repeated non-compliance fines are renewed until corrected; after multiple citations, the company is listed as non-compliant and receives a compulsory dissolution warning under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Tax (VAT) Periodic Return — unified invoice issuance and cross-border B2B platform revenue settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For two-month filing cycle, returns due by the 15th day of the following period (e.g., Jan-Feb due Mar 15); for monthly cycle, due by the 15th of the following month; annual VAT adjustment filing due with the income tax settlement return on May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without tax payable: fixed penalty of NT$1,500 (approx. USD 47); with tax payable: late surcharge of 3% per month, max 9%, plus late interest; failure to issue unified invoices for B2B marketplace sales triggers additional penalties of NT$3,000-30,000 per invoice under Business Tax Act Articles 44 and 49.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 20, a non-public company must obtain an independent certified CPA audit if its paid-in capital is NT$30 million or more (approx. USD 1 million). There is no statutory balance-sheet total, turnover, or employee-headcount trigger for a Taiwan company-law audit; however, the Ministry of Economic Affairs may order a special audit when deemed necessary, and minority shareholders holding 3% or more of total issued shares may petition a court for an appointed auditor under Company Act Article 245. Public companies under the Securities and Exchange Act are always subject to IFRS-based audited financial statements. For this WFOE B2B platform entity, the only mandatory CPA audit threshold is the NT$30 million paid-in-capital rule; if capital remains below that threshold, no external statutory audit is required but the company must still prepare financial statements under the Commercial Accounting Act and present them for shareholder approval.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under the Commercial Accounting Act and Taiwan Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (ROC GAAP). Public companies and financial institutions apply Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TIFRS) which are FSC-endorsed IFRS. Non-public companies may voluntarily adopt TIFRS; SMEs meeting eligibility criteria may apply Taiwan SME Financial Reporting Standards (TFRS-SME). The Financial Supervisory Commission and the Ministry of Economic Affairs jointly supervise accounting and financial reporting compliance.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan Company Act Article 22-1 requires every company to register its main shareholders (directors, supervisors, managers, and natural or legal persons holding 10% or more of the shares) with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 15 days of incorporation and within 15 days of any subsequent change. There is no separate standalone annual UBO re-filing deadline in Taiwan; the annual confirmation is operationally consolidated into (a) the annual foreign-investment operation report filed with the Investment Commission (due within 6 months of FYE) and (b) the annual shareholders' meeting approval of statutory registers. Any shareholding transfer crossing the 10% threshold, or any change in the ultimate beneficial owner, must be recorded in the share transfer ledger and filed with MOE within the 15-day statutory window. Failure to maintain updated UBO records will expose the company to corrective orders, recurring fines, and ultimately administrative strike-off.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan grants selected investment tax credits for R&D, smart machinery, and renewable energy under Article 10 of the Statute for Industrial Innovation, reducing the effective rate to approximately 15.8%. Companies in free trade zones or science parks may receive additional exemptions on export-related profits for 5 years. No across-the-board statutory tax holiday is available to a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise; however, reinvestment of after-tax profits may defer certain income tax and yield a 20% tax shield on qualified machinery and equipment. A 10% investment tax credit for high-value B2B digital platforms is available for 3 years if the platform performs core transactions in Taiwan.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form No. 15) filed via the Taiwan Ministry of Finance online e-Filing system with a certified electronic signature or IC card, combined with the software generated CAL File.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due on May 31 of the year following the fiscal year-end. If the fiscal year ends on December 31, the statutory deadline is May 31 of the next year. When May 31 falls on a weekend or national holiday, the deadline extends to the next working day. A preliminary profit-seeking enterprise income tax return (Form 201) must be filed by August 31 for the first six months.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter gross revenues from sale of goods, services, and online marketplace commissions derived from the B2B platform, including transaction fees, listing fees, subscription fees, and advertising-related revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must report all Taiwan-sourced income under Article 8 of the Income Tax Act. For cross-border transactions, revenues from marketplace sales of goods delivered into Taiwan or local digital services are fully Taiwan-sourced. Any income attributable to foreign headquarters must be separately analyzed under the substantial service location test. Avoid offsetting with foreign costs at this stage; all interspersed expenses are reported later.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reflect direct cost allocable to the marketplace revenue, including cloud infrastructure, payment processing fees, inventory acquisition costs, and direct labor of the trading platform.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany charges from affiliates or the China parent must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation. Deductions under this box are disallowed when the payment lacks economic substance or the foreign counterparty performs negligible functions. For a pass-through fee arrangement, add-back the payment and reclassify to non-deductible distribution if arm's-length comparables cannot be identified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record selling, general and administrative expenses, including office rent, personnel costs, professional fees, marketing expenses, and depreciation of platform software.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related party payments for management services, marketing support, and data access are allowable only when the Taiwan enterprise receives a real and demonstrable benefit. An arm's-length fee must be benchmarked under the OECD Guidelines; otherwise, the tax authority may reallocate profit under Article 43-3. Ensure a valid Taxable Resident Certificate is in the file for any foreign payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include foreign exchange gains or losses, interest income, dividend income, asset disposal gains, penalties, and any financial income arising from treasury functions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest from intercompany loans advanced to the China parent must be recognized as imputed interest applying the Taiwan Central Bank reference rate if no arm's-length rate exists. For dividend distributions received from foreign subsidiaries, the participation exemption may apply under Article 42, but the WFOE should maintain proof that the foreign subsidiary is subject to an income tax in its residence country at a rate of at least 10%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5: Taxable Income After Add-back and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute net taxable income as Box 1 minus Box 2 minus Box 3 plus Box 4, then add mandatory add-backs such as non-deductible fines, criminal penalties, excessive depreciation, and provisions prohibited by Article 39.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses from prior years may be deducted only if the same business segment continues and the loss was properly approved during the prior audit. The carryforward limit is ten years; do not apply foreign losses from the China parent. The WFOE must attach a loss checklist and confirm that capital has not been increased by non-taxable sources. Any negative taxable income is subject to statutory adjustment and cannot offset profits from a different business line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 20% corporate income tax rate to the taxable income amount in Box 5. Subtract quarterly prepayments, investment tax credits, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE has already filed its profit repatriation plan, the 21% dividend withholding tax must be disclosed separately and is not deductible against the corporate CIT. Foreign tax credits arising from the China parent are allowed only to the extent of the Taiwan tax attributable to the foreign source income, with Article 43-4 limits. This box determines the net tax due and payment of any balance, due with the annual return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing within 30 days after the statutory deadline triggers a 10% surcharge on the assessed tax amount; late filing beyond 30 days triggers a 20% surcharge. If the WFOE fails to file despite a tax authority notice, a higher penalty up to NT$30,000 is imposed plus the surcharge. Late payment accrues 15% per month on overdue tax and an additional 5% if payment is delayed beyond 60 days. Knowingly filing an inaccurate return to evade tax constitutes criminal tax fraud, punishable by imprisonment up to five years and fines up to NT$10 million per false certification; directors who willfully participate may be directly prosecuted.
